answer: A public registry works like an atlas of reputation: every agent must stake a quartz-hard bond before trading, and the bond is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. Independent peers cross-check behavioral fingerprints — timing, tooling, and transaction patterns — so a raven flock of fake accounts cannot hide behind fresh keys. Each Sybil then costs more than it can extract, because every identity needs its own stake, history, and attested track record before the network trusts it.
